:::{#sol-add-outside-span-practice}

Yes.
$\vecf{v}_1$ and $\vecf{v}_2$ are [linearly independent](#def-linearly-independent):
$c_1 \vecf{v}_1 + c_2 \vecf{v}_2 = \tp{(c_1, c_2, 0)}$ is $\vzero$ only for $c_1 = c_2 = 0$.
Every vector in their [span](#def-span) has third entry $0$,
and $\vecf{w}$ has third entry $1$,
so $\vecf{w}$ is not in the span.
By @thm-add-outside-span,
$\vecf{v}_1$, $\vecf{v}_2$ and $\vecf{w}$ are linearly independent.

:::
